material_definitions: The samples belong to the solid solution series Li(4-2x)MgxTi(5-x)/3O4 with 0 ≤ x ≤ 1.
The materials were prepared by conventional solid-state reaction using Li2CO3, MgO, and TiO2.
Mixtures were calcined at 800 °C and then sintered into pellets at 1050 °C in air for 24 hours.
Ionic conductivity was determined via AC impedance spectroscopy using a Solartron 1260 analyzer.
Conductivity measurements were conducted over a temperature range of 25 to 400 °C.

material_definitions: Li4-xMgxTi5-xO12 solid solutions (x = 0-1) were synthesized by a conventional solid-state reaction method.
The materials maintain the cubic (Fd-3m) spinel structure throughout the composition range.
Magnesium ions (Mg2+) substitute for lithium ions (Li+) on the tetrahedral 8a sites and for titanium ions (Ti4+) on the octahedral 16d sites.
The phase-stable materials exhibit enhanced ionic conductivity compared to the parent Li4Ti5O12 spinel.
The activation energy for lithium-ion motion in these solid solutions is approximately 0.4 eV.
Substitution of phosphorus by antimony in the Li3P1-xSbxS4 system leads to a solid solution that crystallizes in a γ-Li3PS4-like structure.
The materials were synthesized via a mechanochemical ball-milling process followed by annealing at 200°C for 1 hour.
Increasing the antimony content x induces structural disorder and expands the unit cell volume.
The composition with x = 0.5 exhibits the highest room-temperature ionic conductivity in this series.
Li3SbS4 is the end-member (x=1) of the substitution series and shows poor ionic conductivity compared to phosphorus-containing compositions.
The lithium argyrodites family of solid electrolytes is explored through aliovalent substitution of phosphorus with germanium.
The material series investigated is Li6+xP1-xGexS5I, which was characterized using X-ray and neutron diffraction, impedance spectroscopy, and NMR.
Substitution in the argyrodite structure induces anion site disorder and significantly reduces the activation barrier for lithium-ion motion.
The optimized composition reaches ionic conductivities of 5.4 mS cm-1 in a cold-pressed state and 18.4 mS cm-1 upon sintering.
This electrolyte was implemented in a thick-electrode solid-state battery showing negligible capacity fade over 150 cycles.
warnings: Temperature not explicitly stated; room temperature assumed.

material_definitions: The class of argyrodites Li6PS5X (X = Cl, Br, I) consists of halide anions forming a face-centered cubic lattice with PS4 tetrahedra and free S2- ions.
The Li6+xP1-xGexS5I series involves aliovalent substitution of Ge4+ for P5+ in the argyrodite structure.
Substituting Ge4+ into Li6PS5I induces anion site-disorder between the S2- and I- positions due to the larger unit cell.
Samples were prepared as cold-pressed pellets and also sintered to investigate the impact of processing on ionic conductivity.
This material series demonstrates that inducing disorder via elemental substitution can significantly lower activation barriers and increase lithium-ion conductivity.
warnings: Temperature inferred as room temperature.

material_definitions: The Li+ superionic argyrodites Li6+xP1-xGexS5I were synthesized with increasing Ge4+/P5+ ratios to study the effect of lithium content on ionic conductivity.
Solid solutions were successfully formed up to a composition of at least Li6.7P0.3Ge0.7S5I, beyond which impurity phases like Li4GeS4 appear.
Temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements were used to characterize the ionic transport properties.
Samples were initially prepared as cold-pressed pellets, with some subsequently sintered at 823 K for ten minutes to improve grain contact and conductivity.
Structural analysis revealed that Ge substitution induces S2-/I- site-disorder and widens diffusion pathways, significantly lowering the activation energy for Li+ migration.
warnings: Temperature taken from Figure 5 caption referencing Nyquist plots.
